a.summary: main's TransactionRecord.sign(int,Signer) throws IllegalArgumentException("Invalid signer index %d for transaction with %d required signers.") when index < 0 || index >= numSigners. v1_tx's BaseTransaction.sign(int,Signer) has no guard at all: it goes straight to Transaction.sign(signer, data, messageOffset(), messageLength(), signatureOffset(index)). signIndexRejectsSlotsOutsideTheRequiredSignerRegion (239-252) fails on both cases — Integer.MIN_VALUE wraps 1 + (index << 6) back to offset 1 and silently signs slot 0 (the test comments on exactly this), and index == numSigners writes 64 bytes past the signature region into the message.

b.summary: main's TransactionRecord.sign(Signer) always resolves the slot via signerIndex(signer) and throws IllegalArgumentException("Failed to find index for signer ...") when the key is not one of the required signers. v1_tx's BaseTransaction.sign(Signer) only searches when numSigners() > 1; for a one-signer transaction it takes the else branch and signs slot 0 with whatever signer it was handed, no key check. singleSignerMustMatchTheRequiredPublicKey (160-162) fails both the assertThrows and the 'rejected signer must not alter the transaction' byte comparison.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
